<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|178|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XIII.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=13|verse=6}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on the Imber Saturday in Sept.}}And he said this similitude, A certaine man had {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The figtree vvith only leaues & no fruite, is the Iewes synagogue, & euery other people or person which hath faith and faire wordes, and no good workes.}}∷ a figtree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking for fruite on it, and found not. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=7}}† And he said to the dresser of the vineyard, Loe it is three yeres since I come seeking for fruite vpon this figtree: and I finde not. Cut it dovvne therfore: vvhereto doth it also occupie the ground? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=8}}† But he answering saith to him, Lord, let it alone this yere also, vntil I digge about it, and dung it. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=9}}† and if happily it yeld fruite: but if not, hereafter thou shalt cut it dovvne.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=10}}† And he vvas teaching in their synagogue on the Sabboths. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=11}}† And behold a vvoman that had a spirit of infirmitie eightene yeres: and she vvas crooked neither could she looke vpvvard at al. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=12}}† Whom vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} savv, he called her vnto him, and said to her, Woman, thou art deliuered from thy infirmitie. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=13}}† And he imposed hands vpon her, and forthvvith she vvas made straight and glorified God. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=14}}† And the Archsynagogue ansvvering (because he had indignation that {{sc|Iesvs}} had cured on the Sabboth) said to the multitude, Sixe daies there are vvherein you ought to vvorke. in them therfore come, and be cured: and not in the Sabboth day. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=15}}† And our Lord ansvvering to him, said, Hypocrite, doth not euery one of you vpon the Sabboth loose his oxe or his asse from the manger, and leadeth them to vvater? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=16}}† But {{sup|‖}} this daughter of Abraham vvhom Satan hath bound, loe, these eightene yeres, ought not she to be loosed from this bond on the Sabboth day? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=17}}† And vvhen he said these things, al his aduersaries vvere ashamed: and al the people reioyced in al things that vvere gloriously done of him.⊣

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=18}}† He said therfore, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 13, 31. Mr. 4, 30.''}}* VVherevnto is the kingdom of God like, and vvherevnto shal I esteeme it like? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=19}}† It is like to a {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See Annota. Matth. ''13, 31''.}}∷ mustard seede, vvhich a man tooke and cast into his garden, and it grevv: and became a great tree, and the foules of the aire rested in the boughes thereof. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=20}}† And againe he said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 13, 33.''}}* Like to vvhat shal I esteeme the kingdom of God? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=21}}† It is like to leauen, vvhich a vvoman tooke and hid in three measures of meale, til the vvhole vvas leauened. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=22}}† And he vvent by cities and tovvnes teaching, and making his iourney vnto Hierusalem.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=23}}† And a certaine man said to him, Lord, be they fevv that are saued? {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 7, 13.''}}* But he said to them, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=24}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christians in their liues must seeke the strait way, but in religion the ancient common way.}}∷ Striue to enter {{sup|‖}} by the narrow gate: because many, I say to you, {{sup|‖}} shal seeke to enter,<noinclude>{{rh|||and}}</noinclude>
